subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class named session snapshots now, and what initial scope should be supported: arbitrary save/list/load, archive restore, compaction checkpoint branch/restore, prompt-cache-aware fork, or a staged subset?
rationale: Current main has several adjacent primitives but no unified contract for restore destructiveness, retention, privacy, archive import, or fork semantics, and automation should not choose that product/API boundary.

options.title: Design core snapshot API first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a versioned contract for named checkpoints, branch/load behavior, retention, privacy, protocol, commands, UI/CLI exposure, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to resume/archive restore
options.body: Let a smaller restore-oriented path land first while keeping named checkpoint save/load and deterministic fork semantics tracked separately.

options.title: Defer named snapshots
options.body: Keep compaction checkpoints, export commands, and session fork primitives separate until stronger maintainer demand justifies a unified snapshot surface.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshot API first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define a versioned contract for named checkpoints, branch/load behavior, retention, privacy, protocol, commands, UI/CLI exposure, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent product-review signal on this issue and current session-area history.
